A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their complete main texts, appendices, equations, tables, and figures are readable and support comparison, including matching material moved between sections.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification experiments on Pl@ntNet-300K and iNaturalist, including truncated datasets, method analyses, endangered-species results, and simulated human decision accuracy.

after.justification: v2 reports original results on the same datasets and simulations, with revised experimental results and an additional focal-loss experiment.

M1.justification: PAS, WPAS, INTERP-Q, and FUZZY remain present despite relocation. v2 Appendix A.2 corrects FUZZY's reconformalization rule to include equality at the calibrated transformed-score threshold and specifies an epsilon adjustment when implementing it through Raw FUZZY. This refines the procedure stated in v1 Section 2.2.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Pl@ntNet-300K and iNaturalist-2018, their truncated variants with 330 and 857 classes, endangered-species coverage, and verifier/guesser decision scenarios. The added focal-loss experiment changes the classifier configuration, not dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: EXACT CLASSWISE remains in the comprehensive softmax comparison, moving from v1 Figure 4 to v2 Figure 7. However, it disappears from the corresponding PAS-score comparison in v1 Figure 7 versus v2 Figure 9. STANDARD, CLASSWISE, and CLUSTERED remain in that comparison.

E3.justification: v1 Appendix B.2 uses the same validation data for epoch selection and conformal calibration. v2 Appendices C.1–C.2 instead reserve random, disjoint 30% and 70% portions for those purposes, substantially changing the evaluation design. v2 also adds focal-loss training and revises INTERP-Q and WPAS parameter sweeps; the 20-epoch budget and learning rate remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The supplementary analyses are substantially revised. v2 adds a focal-loss robustness check and expands simulated INTERP-Q decision accuracy from one interpolation setting to ten settings. It removes FUZZY's decision-accuracy analysis and the truncated-dataset panels from the class-mapping and PAS-combination analyses, while retaining those analyses on the full datasets.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, experimental seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The displayed verifier/guesser ranges represent alternative decision behaviors rather than statistical uncertainty, and no uncertainty-reporting practice is introduced.

E6.justification: Benchmark and case-study results are revised, with additional focal-loss and interpolation-sensitivity results. For example, PAS coverage for Abeliophyllum distichum changes from 1.00 to 0.00, and for Vanilla planifolia from 1.00 to 0.80 (v1 Figure 9; v2 Figure 12). These are replaced results under the revised experimental protocol, not established same-setting performance declines. The broad size-versus-coverage conclusions remain similar.

T1.justification: v2 Proposition 3 and Appendix B.3 introduce a proof that INTERP-Q achieves marginal coverage of at least 1−2α; v1 explicitly says it lacks a coverage guarantee. v2 also revises FUZZY's coverage statement and supplies the strict-versus-nonstrict threshold argument in Appendix B.5. The weighted-PAS optimality theorem and existing FUZZY results are otherwise retained.

C1.justification: The abstract's second principal contribution changes from label-weighted conformal prediction to linear quantile interpolation. INTERP-Q is now presented as a method with a marginal coverage guarantee, replacing v1's explicit absence-of-guarantee claim. FUZZY remains an alternative in the appendix, while PAS and the overall long-tailed coverage objective are retained.

C2.justification: v2 explains INTERP-Q's nonlinear set-size response through rare-class score distributions, states that FUZZY does not empirically outperform simpler INTERP-Q, and acknowledges an exchangeability issue when tuning on calibration data. It removes v1's explicit limitation concerning balanced datasets. The main interpretations of coverage and decision accuracy remain broadly similar.

D1.justification: v2 adds the focal-loss implementation source and parameters γ=2 and α=1, plus FUZZY's epsilon-adjustment instructions. Conversely, it omits v1's explicit FUZZY bandwidth rescaling σy=σ/(ny+1) and experimental bandwidth grid, despite retaining FUZZY results. The main code-access information, hardware, and basic training details remain.

R1.justification: v2 adds Lin et al. on focal loss, Menon et al. on logit adjustment, and Shumailov et al. on model collapse, modestly expanding the positioning against class-imbalance research. The weighted-conformal discussion and its references move into Appendix A rather than disappearing.

P1.justification: The narrative is extensively reorganized and edited. FUZZY moves from the main methods section to Appendix A, while weighted macro-coverage and endangered-species experiments move into the main text. Preliminaries, method summaries, experimental explanations, discussion, and appendix organization are substantially rewritten around PAS and INTERP-Q.

P2.justification: v2 adds Algorithm 1, a method-summary table, numerical results Tables 3–4, and the focal-loss figure. It separates the simpler main comparison from the comprehensive appendix figure and redraws decision-accuracy plots as panels for different verifier probabilities, with method-specific class ordering. Numerous figures also change placement, styling, legends, and captions.

improvement.justification: The separate epoch-selection and calibration split resolves v1's acknowledged data reuse that conflicted with a central conformal assumption. Together with INTERP-Q's new coverage bound and the corrected FUZZY formulation, this substantially strengthens the paper's rigor; the focal-loss check adds useful support. These gains outweigh limited losses in supplementary detail and a new reporting inconsistency: Section 3.1 attributes set sizes 7.6 and 55.8 to τ=0.99, whereas Tables 3–4 assign them to τ=0.999.
